name: Consistencia de Entidades Nombradas
description: Evaluates the consistency and factual accuracy of named entities (people, places, dates) to detect AI hallucinations and fabricated content.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated text through inconsistent or hallucinated named entities
mechanism: Extracts named entities using NER models, then checks for internal consistency (same entity referenced with conflicting attributes), temporal plausibility (dates and events alignment), and cross-referencing density. AI-generated text is prone to 'hallucination'—generating plausible-sounding but factually incorrect entity mentions or mixing attributes between different entities.
source: Ji, Z. et al. (2023) - Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation, ACM Computing Surveys
algorithm: Named Entity Recognition + Consistency Graph + Conflict Detection
parameters: NER model: transformer-based, Entity types: PER/ORG/LOC/DATE/NUM, Consistency check: pairwise attribute comparison, Threshold: adaptive per entity type
strengths:
• Directly targets AI hallucination problem
• High precision on factual documents
• Interpretable error examples
• Effective on news and academic text
limitations:
• Requires domain knowledge for fact-checking
• Creative fiction has naturally inconsistent entities
• NER model errors propagate to analysis
• Less useful for opinion or abstract text

references.title: Ji, Z. et al. (2023). Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation. ACM Computing Surveys.
Manakul, P. et al. (2023). SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative LLMs. EMNLP.
